content.title: Alstom secures maintenance contract for 62 Mälartåg trains in Sweden
content.summary: The agreement, which could extend for up to 10 years, is scheduled to commence with Alstom taking over maintenance responsibilities in December 2026.

thumbnail.caption: The contract will use Alstom's Maintenance Performance Centre in the Nordic region to coordinate maintenance for various train fleets. Credit: Alstom SA.

content.title: Eurostar places €2bn order for 50 Alstom double-decker high-speed rolling stock
content.summary: The new rolling stock, dubbed Eurostar Celestia, is based on Alstom’s Avelia Horizon platform.

thumbnail.caption: Rendering of a Eurostar Celestia train at London St-Pancras International station. Credit: Alstom

content.title: Eurostar plans double-decker train amid competition threat
content.summary: Eurostar said Wednesday it will run double-decker trains through the Channel Tunnel for the first time, as it faces potential competition on its routes between London and mainland Europe."We're particularly proud to bring double-decker trains to the UK for the very first time," she added in a statement.

thumbnail.caption: The new double-decker trains will begin to enter service in 2031 (Stefano RELLANDINI)

content.title: First major fleet of double-decker trains to run on UK railways
content.summary: Eurostar has confirmed an initial order for 30 trains, and has an option for a further 20.

content.title: Eurostar orders UK’s first fleet of double-decker trains
content.summary: A major fleet of double-decker trains is to operate in Britain for the first time, but passengers have been warned not to expect twice as many seats. Eurostar said it will purchase up to 50 two-storey trains from Alstom for use on routes including London St Pancras International to Paris, Brussels and Amsterdam via the Channel Tunnel.

thumbnail.caption: Picture of what the Eurostar Celestia will look like

content.title: Did Alstom's (ENXTPA:ALO) New CEO Appointment Signal a Strategic Shift for the Company?
content.summary: Alstom’s Board of Directors has selected Martin Sion to become the company’s new Chief Executive Officer, effective April 1, 2026, succeeding Henri Poupart-Lafarge who has served since 2016 and will remain in his position to ensure a smooth transition. This leadership change introduces an executive with extensive aerospace and industrial experience, marking a significant shift as Alstom continues to pursue growth and operational improvement.
